abstract: Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) is a major crop grown on about 225 million hectares worldwide, and it suffers heavy losses from rusts caused by fungal pathogens. This study focuses on leaf rust, caused by Puccinia triticina. When wheat is attacked by this fungus, hundreds of downstream genes in various biological pathways show regulated expression, which depends partly on non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs) and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). Because lncRNAs are both regulators and sources of miRNAs, understanding lncRNA-miRNA relationships is important for understanding gene regulation. RNA-seq data from the EMBL-EBI archive were quality-checked with FastQC, aligned with HISAT2 and assembled with StringTie. Transcripts shorter than 200 nucleotides (nt) and other ncRNAs (rRNA, tRNA and snoRNA) were removed, and coding potential was assessed with CPC2 and PLEK, followed by BLASTX against Pfam to remove protein-coding sequences. Differential expression was analysed with NOISeq, and lncRNA-miRNA interactions were predicted with psRNATarget. In total, 7,390 presumed lncRNAs were identified, of which 5,496 were differentially expressed in susceptible and resistant wheat lines. LncRNA targets of 59 miRNAs were analysed; these miRNAs have been reported to regulate plant disease-related genes such as the SPL and NAC families and the cyclophilins TaCYP61, TaCYP62, TaCYP43, TaCYP76 and TaCYP81.
